observations: Photo 0 shows a black flat-screen monitor on a stand, placed on a tiled floor against a speckled wall. The screen is off and reflects the surroundings. A power adapter and cables are visible beneath the monitor.

Photo 1 shows the back of the monitor. The LG logo is visible at the top center. Below it, there is a rectangular panel with ports (likely HDMI, VGA, etc.) and a small label. The stand is attached to the bottom center. Cables are bundled and connected to the back.
The monitor appears to be a standard desktop display, not a TV, based on size and stand design.
No visible damage to the screen or casing in either photo.
The seller claims it is a 32-inch LG monitor working perfectly fine.

claims.evidence: LG logo is visible on the back in photo 1. The size is not directly readable but is consistent with the visual proportions of a 32-inch monitor in photo 0.
No photo shows the monitor powered on or displaying an image. The power adapter is present, but no proof of functionality is shown.

risks.risk: Monitor may not work or may have dead pixels, screen burn, or other display issues.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the monitor powered on with a clear, full-screen image.

risks.risk: The monitor may have physical damage not visible in the photos, such as cracks or scratches on the screen.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the screen surface under direct light, showing the entire screen area.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having minor cosmetic damage

risks.risk: The monitor may be missing essential accessories (e.g., HDMI cable, stand, or power cord) or have damaged ports.
risks.proof: A clear photo of all ports on the back and a photo of the included cables and accessories.

proof_requests: A photo or video of the monitor turned on, displaying a clear image.
A close-up photo of the screen surface under direct light to check for scratches or dead pixels.
A photo of all included cables and accessories, including the power cord and any connectors.
response.reason: The monitor is identifiable as an LG brand, and the size is plausible, but functionality and condition cannot be confirmed without proof of operation and screen integrity. The claim of 'working perfectly fine' is unverified, and hidden risks like dead pixels or missing accessories affect pricing. Proof is needed before pricing.
